newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD-HK stocks seen firm, focus on red chips.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-HK stocks seen firm, focus on red chips.

text.p: Excitement surrounding Hong Kong's most popular IPO ever is set to give share prices a lift this coming week and investors are likely to seize any weakness as a buying opportunity, analysts said.

China-backed Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd is due to make its market debut on Thursday, fuelling the market's craze for red-chips, or Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China.
Blue chips are also expected to be well supported by rotational buying, analysts said.
"At this high level, it is a bull and bear battle but the overall market tone remains quite firm," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.

The Hang Seng Index continued to hit record highs last week, scoring an all-time intra-day high of 14,398.55 points last Wednesday and setting a record close of 14,331.68 on Friday. The index gained 269.31 points, or 1.92 percent, over the week.
Analysts said new records on Wall Street were likely to boost sentiment further. The Dow industrials rose 87.78 points to a record close of 7,345.91 on Friday.
"For the upside we are looking at 14,500," Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International, said of the Hang Seng.
But he said if the blue-chip index breached that level, he would issue a sell recommendation.
"The market is extremely overbought at this level. I don't think we will sustain this kind of level," said Tang.

Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities, said the Hang Seng Index had established support at 14,150 points and any dips to around that level would be met with buying, particularly in laggard stocks.
"A lot of people are waiting on the sidelines to jump in the market. When the property sector weakens, buying comes in."
Analysts said red-chip stocks would be a focus.
"We are likely to see some of the hot plays get hotter. It is just a theme which brokers and fund managers like," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.

Hong Kong investors queued up for hours last week to get in on the latest red-chip initial public offering (IPO). Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's Hong Kong public offering was expected to be 1,000 to 1,500 times subscribed, the highest ever in the territory.
The company sold 150 million shares in a global initial public offering. Ten percent was offered in Hong Kong and 90 percent to international investors.
"Beijing Enterprises epitomises the perfect China red chip in terms of connections and businesses," said Rossiter.

Controlled by the Beijing municipal government, the conglomerate owns a stake in Beijing McDonald's, the company which operates the fast-food chain in the city. It also has interests in brewing, toll roads, hotels and retailing.
The stock is expected to soar with the grey market price quoted at HK$38-HK$39 on Friday compared with an issue price of HK$12.48.
Lee & Man Holdings is also due to make its market debut on Wednesday. The handbag and cardboard maker offered 206.25 million shares at HK$1.00 per share.
